Investment Thesis
Brand strength paired with a wholesale-led marketplace reset
• NIKE operates one of the world’s most recognized portfolios of athletic footwear, apparel and equipment brands.
• Management is rebalancing marketplace execution while investing in sport, product innovation and brand demand creation.
• FY2026 revenue reached $52.8 billion, supported by wholesale growth and stabilization across core geographies.
• The company remains globally diversified, with North America as its largest profit contributor.
• Converse remains part of the portfolio and provides an additional lifestyle-oriented consumer brand.

Operating Footprint
Global distribution with a scaled employee base
• NIKE is headquartered at One Bowerman Drive in Beaverton, Oregon.
• The company employs approximately 81,500 people worldwide.
• NIKE is incorporated in Delaware and operates through a global network of subsidiaries.
• Its marketplace spans wholesale partners, NIKE-owned retail stores and digital commerce.
• The company sells across North America, Europe/Middle East/Africa, Greater China, and Asia Pacific/Latin America.
NIKE, Inc. — Zelda Intelligence Suite controlled test deck

Marketplace Momentum
Wholesale improvement offsets pressure in direct channels
• FY2026 wholesale revenue increased 6% on a reported basis.
• NIKE Direct revenue declined 6% on a reported basis.
• NIKE Brand Digital revenue increased 8% during FY2026.
• Converse revenue declined materially during the year.
• North America remained a major source of NIKE Brand earnings.

Key Risks
Execution, channel mix and global consumer exposure
• Continued weakness in digital demand could pressure the pace of NIKE Direct recovery.
• Tariffs, foreign exchange movements and sourcing costs can affect gross margin.
• Greater China remains an important market where demand volatility can affect consolidated performance.
• Competitive intensity in athletic footwear and apparel requires sustained innovation and marketing investment.
• Portfolio performance at Converse remains a watch item following significant revenue declines.

Can the evidence layer separate supported facts from contradictions and unknowns?

• Does the stated employee count match the latest available company disclosure?
• Is the claimed state of incorporation consistent with SEC issuer metadata?
• Are channel-growth statements supported by reported results?
• Does Zelda preserve correct facts while flagging only claims its evidence can actually contradict?
